acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Nagas family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Coilguard, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Twin-Blade Coil Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Longer patterned coils, twin curved daggers, and simple gold bands mature the baseline while retaining two arms and no hood.
Signature mechanic: Crossed Crescent: the two-armed, hoodless Coilguard plants patterned coils and sweeps twin daggers from the outer curve toward one crossing point.
battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable curved front line by bracing longer coils and threatening opposite arcs with two curved daggers.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 retain no hood and two arms with sail-cut sashes and flute cuffs; T3–T5 retain hood and multiple arms with pressure vanes mounted only on existing hood ribs, sashes, and weapon bands.
Movement gains directional pressure through hollow gold flutes, aligned silk streamers, vented scale bands, sequential hand vanes, and a still center at the active coil knot or hood hinge.
counterplay: Enter the coil interior before the blades cross or strike the flattened outer scale row to break the brace. Affinity signal: Sashes and hand vanes align toward one lane while the active coil knot becomes perfectly still; cross the lee or strike that knot before release.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only pale scales without flutes, vanes, and directional pressure
Glow-only wind treatment without a force route and still center
Invented early-tier hoods or extra arms for wind silhouettes
Floating that removes coil contact and readable load
identityInvariants: A humanoid torso rises from a long coiled serpent body; the T1–T2 forms have two arms and no hood, while hood and additional arms begin only at T3.
Emerald, jade, deep teal, gold, bronze, ivory, and jewel-toned scale patterns remain the family palette.
Scale, gold, gemstone inlay, silk sash, and temple stone remain separate readable materials rather than a seamless magical body.
Arm bands, gold scale bands, jeweled brow pieces, sacred script, and later hood crests communicate rank.
Coil direction, weapon-bearing hands, hood angle where present, and exposed scale seams preserve attack and counterplay readability.
telegraph: Simple gold arm bands touch, both curved blades turn inward, and the patterned outer coil flattens against the floor.
